title: Electrical Site Engineer
description:
Company: Quality Council of India (QCI) Experience: 5-8 Years Qualification: B.Tech / M.Tech in Electrical Engineering. Job Locations: Gorakhpur, Nagpur & Ahmedabad 
 About the Company: Quality Council of India (QCI) is a premier autonomous body set up by the Government of India. QCI is responsible for creating a Quality Mindset and envisions to ensure quality across products and services that touch every citizen. As an independent and autonomous body, QCI creates a mechanism for independent third-party assessments of products, services, and processes, coordinating its activities through its constituent boards and divisions. The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce & Industry, serves as the nodal point for QCI. 
 About the Role: We are looking for an experienced Electrical Site Inspector / Engineer with at least 5 years of experience in electrical site execution, inspection, and quality control. 
 Responsibilities: Monitor daily electrical site work and ensure quality and safety standards. Inspect electrical installations and identify defects or mistakes. Check that work is carried out as per approved drawings and specifications. Ensure compliance with relevant Indian Standards (IS Codes) and safety rules. Prepare inspection reports with photographs and observations. Coordinate with contractors and project teams to resolve site issues. Follow up on corrective actions to ensure timely completion. 
 Qualifications: B.Tech / B.E. in Electrical Engineering. 
 Required Skills: 515 years of overall experience. Minimum 5 years of experience in electrical site execution, inspection, or quality control. Knowledge of electrical construction practices and safety standards. Good understanding of Indian Standards (IS Codes). Good reporting, communication, and coordination skills. Ability to identify and resolve technical issues at site.

title: Sr Executive
description:
SUMMARY 
 Job Description Purchase Executive / Manager CAPEX Procurement 
 Position 
 Purchase Executive / Manager CAPEX 
 Department 
 Purchase / Procurement 
 Industry 
 Pharmaceutical Manufacturing 
 Location 
 Nagpur / Butibori 
 Reporting To 
 Head Purchase / Procurement Head 
 
 1. Job Purpose 
 To manage end-to-end procurement of CAPEX materials, machinery, equipment, utilities, engineering items and project-related requirements for pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities, ensuring optimum cost, quality, timely delivery and compliance with approved specifications and company procedures. 
 
 2. Key Responsibilities 
 A. CAPEX Procurement 
 Handle complete procurement of CAPEX equipment and project materials from RFQ to final delivery. 
 Procure pharmaceutical manufacturing equipment such as: 
 Reactors 
 Manufacturing vessels 
 Storage tanks 
 Homogenizers 
 Mixers 
 Pumps 
 HVAC equipment 
 Stability chambers 
 BOD incubators 
 Tablet compression machines 
 Vibro sifters 
 Utility equipment 
 Electrical panels and equipment 
 SS/HDPE/PP/FRP equipment 
 Piping, valves and engineering materials. 
 Purchase MS, SS304, SS316/316L, HDPE, PP, FRP and other engineering materials as per approved specifications. 
 Understand BOQ, URS, technical specifications, GA drawings and vendor offers before floating RFQs. 
 B. Vendor Development & Management 
 Identify and develop reliable manufacturers and suppliers for CAPEX requirements. 
 Maintain an updated approved / qualified vendor database . 
 Obtain quotations from multiple vendors and ensure competitive bidding. 
 Evaluate vendor capability, manufacturing capacity, previous pharma references and service support. 
 Negotiate: 
 Price 
 Payment terms 
 Delivery 
 Warranty 
 Freight 
 Installation 
 Commissioning 
 AMC 
 Spare parts 
 Documentation. 
 C. Technical & Commercial Evaluation 
 Prepare Technical & Commercial Comparative Statements (CSQ) . 
 Compare quotations on a like-for-like basis . 
 Identify deviations, exclusions, optional items and hidden costs in vendor quotations. 
 Coordinate with Engineering, Projects, QA, Production and other departments for technical evaluation. 
 Identify cases where vendors have proposed non-BOQ / higher-cost alternatives and challenge them where technically acceptable alternatives already exist. 
 Verify: 
 Material of construction 
 Thickness 
 Capacity 
 Dimensions 
 Motor rating 
 Make 
 Design pressure 
 Design temperature 
 Utility requirements 
 Performance parameters 
 Testing requirements. 
 D. Cost Control & Negotiation 
 Establish market-rate benchmarks for CAPEX materials and equipment. 
 Conduct price negotiations with vendors and achieve maximum cost savings. 
 Compare current vendor rates with: 
 Previous purchase rates 
 Market rates 
 Alternative vendors 
 Approved BOQ rates 
 Budgeted CAPEX values. 
 Prepare cost-saving and negotiation reports . 
 Identify opportunities for: 
 Rate reduction 
 Payment-term improvement 
 Freight optimization 
 Standardization 
 Alternate vendors 
 Bulk procurement. 
 E. Project Procurement 
 Prepare procurement schedules based on project requirements. 
 Track long-lead items and ensure timely ordering. 
 Coordinate with Project/Engineering teams regarding: 
 URS 
 RFQ 
 Technical clarifications 
 Drawing approval 
 PO release 
 Manufacturing 
 FAT 
 Dispatch 
 Installation 
 SAT 
 Commissioning. 
 Closely monitor critical project equipment to avoid project delays. 
 F. Change Control & Variation Management 
 Review vendor change-control requests, variation statements and price escalation claims . 
 Verify whether the claimed change is actually outside the original PO/BOQ scope. 
 Recalculate: 
 Material quantity 
 Weight increase 
 Rate impact 
 Fabrication charges 
 Additional accessories. 
 Challenge unsupported additional-cost claims. 
 Ensure no commercial amendment is approved without proper technical justification and management approval. 
 G. Purchase Order Management 
 Prepare and release purchase orders after final approval. 
 Ensure PO contains: 
 Approved technical specification 
 Scope of supply 
 Price 
 GST 
 Freight 
 Payment terms 
 Delivery period 
 Warranty 
 LD clause 
 Inspection/FAT requirements 
 Documentation requirements. 
 Track PO commitments and vendor delivery schedules. 
 Coordinate amendments wherever technically or commercially required. 
 H. Quality & Documentation 
 Ensure required documentation is obtained from vendors, including where applicable: 
 GA drawings 
 Manufacturing drawings 
 BOM 
 Material Test Certificates 
 Calibration certificates 
 Test certificates 
 Inspection reports 
 FAT protocols/reports 
 IQ/OQ/PQ documents 
 DQ documents 
 Welding certificates 
 Pressure/vacuum test certificates 
 MOC certificates 
 Operation & Maintenance manuals 
 Warranty certificates 
 Spare-parts lists. 
 I. Vendor Performance 
 Monitor vendors against: 
 Quality 
 Cost 
 Delivery 
 Responsiveness 
 Documentation 
 Technical compliance 
 After-sales support. 
 Maintain a Vendor Performance Rating and recommend corrective action or replacement where required. 
 3. Key KPIs 
 KPI 
 Measurement 
 CAPEX Cost Saving 
 Actual saving vs budget / quoted price 
 Purchase Price Variance 
 PO rate vs benchmark/previous rate 
 RFQ Coverage 
 Minimum 3 competitive quotations wherever practical 
 On-Time Delivery 
 % CAPEX orders delivered within committed date 
 Vendor Development 
 Number of qualified alternate vendors developed 
 Payment-Term Improvement 
 Improvement from advance to PDC/credit terms 
 Change-Control Saving 
 Amount prevented/reduced against vendor claims 
 Technical Compliance 
 % orders meeting approved specification 
 CSQ Accuracy 
 Technical & commercial deviations correctly identified 
 Project Procurement Completion 
 Procurement completed as per project schedule 
 Emergency Purchase 
 Reduction in emergency / last-minute procurement 
 Documentation Compliance 
 % orders with complete required documentation 
 
 4. Required Skills 
 Strong knowledge of CAPEX procurement 
 Knowledge of pharmaceutical manufacturing equipment 
 Ability to read and understand BOQ, URS, GA drawings and technical specifications 
 Strong commercial negotiation skills 
 Vendor development 
 Cost analysis and market-rate benchmarking 
 Technical & commercial comparison 
 Knowledge of MS/SS/HDPE/PP/FRP materials 
 Knowledge of pumps, tanks, reactors, machinery, utilities and engineering equipment 
 Excel / ERP / procurement software proficiency 
 Strong coordination with Engineering, Projects, QA and Finance. 
 
 5. Preferred Experience 
 Experience: 5 10 years in Purchase/Procurement, preferably in: 
 Pharmaceutical manufacturing 
 API / formulation plants 
 Chemical manufacturing 
 Engineering projects 
 Pharma CAPEX procurement. 
 Experience in greenfield/brownfield pharmaceutical projects will be preferred. 
 
 6. Educational Qualification 
 Preferred: 
 B.E./B.Tech Mechanical / Production / Industrial Engineering 
 Diploma in Mechanical Engineering with strong CAPEX procurement experience 
 MBA/PG Diploma in Supply Chain / Procurement will be an advantage. 
 
 7. Core Competencies 
 Commercial negotiation 
 Analytical thinking 
 Cost consciousness 
 Technical understanding 
 Vendor management 
 Decision making 
 Project coordination 
 Problem solving 
 Documentation discipline 
 Communication skills 
 
 
 Requirements Strong knowledge of CAPEX procurement 
 Knowledge of pharmaceutical manufacturing equipment 
 Ability to read and understand BOQ, URS, GA drawings and technical specifications 
 Strong commercial negotiation skills 
 Vendor development 
 Cost analysis and market-rate benchmarking

 Knowledge of MS/SS/HDPE/PP/FRP materials 
 Knowledge of pumps, tanks, reactors, machinery, utilities and engineering equipment

 Strong coordination with Engineering, Projects, QA and Finance.
